top_choice_rationale: P001 is an original, experimentally verified discovery: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a specific, falsifiable magic-angle prediction and the 2018 Jarillo-Herrero transport work found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle. The phenomena have been reproduced by independent groups using transport and scanning-probe and spectroscopic imaging, and carried to multilayers and moire TMDs, so the award does not hinge on the unsettled pairing mechanism. Twist angle and gate voltage are a new knob that opens a door onto correlated phases, which is the kind of tool-enabled discovery I value. The credit chain (Yuan Cao's omission under the three-name limit, earlier continuum-band work) is a real cost that must be recorded, but Mehlig's reading supports the theory credit and the omission cannot be hidden in the wording. P002 is a close second: it is very well verified and mature, with the cleanest attribution, but it is closer to a refinement of the lineage honoured in 2005 and 2012 than to a new phenomenon. No award ranks last, as both proposals are defensible.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I note only the shared Chalmers/Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Mehlig, with no collaboration with any credited laureate
